title: Delivery Grid

examples.explanation: Down, down, right, right reaches the bottom-right corner in 4 steps.
The robot is walled in at the start.

constraints: every row has the same length

steps.title: Clarify the input
steps.description: Asks which moves are allowed and what to return when the start or destination is blocked or unreachable.
look_for: asks about a blocked start or end
hints: Before you start, is there anything about how the robot moves that you'd want to confirm?
Can the robot move diagonally, and what if the start square itself is blocked?
Confirm 4-direction moves, and settle blocked and unreachable cases before you code.

steps.title: Search outward level by level
steps.description: Uses a queue so squares are explored in order of distance from the start.
look_for: says breadth-first search finds the fewest steps
hints: Look at the order in which you explore squares.
Which search order guarantees the first time you reach a square is by the shortest route?
Breadth-first search with a queue explores squares in order of distance.

steps.title: Mark squares when you add them
steps.description: Records a square as visited when it's added to the queue, so it's never queued twice.
look_for: marks visited before or when enqueuing
hints: Check how many times the same square can end up in your queue.
If two neighbors both find the same square, does it get added twice?
Mark a square visited at the moment you enqueue it.

steps.title: Stay inside the grid and off walls
steps.description: Checks bounds and blocked squares before moving to a neighbor.
hints: Look at what happens at the edge of the grid.
What does your code do with a neighbor that's off the grid or blocked?
Check bounds and skip '#' squares before enqueuing a neighbor.

steps.title: Handle the impossible cases
steps.description: Returns -1 when the start or destination is blocked or the queue empties first, and 0 for a 1x1 open grid.
hints: Try your code where there's no way through.
What happens if the start square is blocked, or the queue runs out?
Return -1 for a blocked start or end, or when the search finishes without reaching it.

common_mistakes.description: uses depth-first search and returns the first path found
common_mistakes.symptom: the first path found is not always the shortest

common_mistakes.description: marks squares visited only when taking them off the queue
common_mistakes.symptom: squares get queued many times; slow on open grids

common_mistakes.description: doesn't check whether the start square is blocked
common_mistakes.symptom: returns 0 or a path for a grid like ["#"]

wrap_up_questions: What are the time and space complexity?
How would you change this if some squares took longer to cross than others?

origin_note: Original. Pattern: breadth-first search from the start.
